newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus denies in Lockheed merger talks.
newsitem.headline: Airbus denies in Lockheed merger talks.

text.p: Airbus denied on Monday a British newspaper report it was in merger talks with U.S. aerospace group Lockheed Martin.
"We deny there are any merger talks with Lockheed," a spokeswoman for the four-nation Airbus Industrie consortium said in response to a Saturday report in the London Times.
The newspaper said the two groups were discussing a merger to confront a growing threat from Boeing in the world market.
Airbus's four partners are at present negotiating changing the partnership into a single integrated company owning its own manufacturing assets and transforming it from a marketing and sales venture.
Airbus is also looking for risk-sharing partners for its project to build a 550-seat airliner which it believes is needed to break U.S.-based Boeing Co's monopoly in that sector.
"We are exploring market opportunities with many aerospace companies worldwide, notably for the large airliner, the A3XX," she said.

In the United States, a source close to Lockheed Martin also dismissed the merger report and added that the U.S. company did not plan to enter as an equity partner in the commercial aircraft business.

An Aerospatiale spokesman said on Saturday any talk of a merger was premature as European aerospace and defence companies needed to complete an industry consolidation as well as transform Airbus into an integrated company before even considering any wider move.

Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc , Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG of Germany, and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
